stemMd: When ammonia accepts a proton from water, which species is its conjugate acid?
explanationMd: A conjugate acid differs from its base by one added proton. NH3 plus H+ gives NH4+, while water loses that proton to become hydroxide.

distractorRationale.b: This is not formed by adding one proton to ammonia.
distractorRationale.d: This has one fewer proton, not one more.
distractorRationale.c: This is molecular hydrogen, not protonated ammonia.
distractorRationale.e: This is the conjugate base of water in the reaction.
